mainTopic: The purification a בעל קרי needs (forty סאה, nine קבין, or nothing), and the משנה's rules about a בעל קרי, foul things, and interruptions during תפלה and שמע
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: רב אסי rules that a sick person with an involuntary emission needs no purification at all. אביי and רבא then give two different histories of how עזרא's enactment of טבילה grew into rules of forty סאה, nine קבין, or nothing. רבא gives the practical הלכה: any normal emission needs forty סאה, a healthy person with an involuntary emission needs nine קבין, and a sick person with an involuntary emission needs nothing. A ברייתא adds that nine קבין is enough for learning alone but forty סאה is needed to teach others, and four אמוראים argue about how to read it. A story about leading ברכת המזון and רב חמא's immersion before פסח show this idea in practice, but the הלכה does not follow רב חמא. Then a new משנה teaches what a בעל קרי does if he remembers in the middle of תפלה, how to say שמע while immersing, and to keep four אמות from foul things. The גמרא discusses צואה near someone praying, and רבה and רבא argue whether a תפלה said near צואה counts. The amud ends with a dispute about where a person resumes after stopping his תפלה, and the גמרא begins to suggest the reason behind it.

steps.title: רב אסי: a sick person with an involuntary emission is fully exempt
steps.stepSummary: A question arose in רב אושעיא's chamber, and רב אסי answered that the nine-קבין rule for a sick person applies only to a normal emission. If the emission was involuntary, he is exempt from everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רב אושעיא's chamber they came and asked רב אסי. He told them: This was only taught about a sick person who had a normal emission. But a sick person whose emission was involuntary is exempt from anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a report from just before this. A question about a sick בעל קרי reached רב אסי, and he answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a teaching that a sick person who had an emission becomes pure with nine קבין poured over him. רב אסי limits it to a normal emission (מרגיל). An involuntary emission (לאונסו) in a sick person needs no purification at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber or hall where the חכמים gathered
A sick person
Having a normal emission, through ordinary marital relations
Involuntarily, against his control
Exempt from anything at all

phrases.english: In the chamber of Rav Oshaya,
they came and asked Rav Asi.
He said to them:
They only taught this about a sick person who had a normal emission,
phrases.notes: "This" means the rule that a sick בעל קרי needs nine קבין of water poured over him.

phrases.english: but a sick person whose emission was involuntary
is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ וּשְׁאִלוּ לְרַב אַסִּי אֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the nine-קבין rule for a sick person cover every kind of emission?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a normal emission. A sick person with an involuntary emission is fully exempt.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב נחמן's jug is useful again
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reacts to רב אסי's ruling by saying that רב נחמן's jug is 'rejoined.' His nine-קבין jug is effective for purification again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב נחמן's jug has been put back together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws a conclusion from רב אסי's answer. רב נחמן's nine-קבין jug is once again a valid way to purify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן kept a jug holding nine קבין for pouring over people. Once רב אסי showed how the nine-קבין rule works, that jug is useful again. The jug is a picture of the whole method being restored.

keyTerms.meaning: Was joined together again, restored
A jug or water jar

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rav Nachman's jug is rejoined.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן kept a jug of nine קבין for pouring. "Rejoined" means it is useful again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אִצְטְמִיד חַצְבֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical conclusion from רב אסי's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The nine-קבין pouring method is valid again.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אסי, a sick person with a normal emission needs nine קבין, and one with an involuntary emission needs nothing. (רבא's final ruling in step 9 is different for a normal emission.)

steps.title: Let's look at what עזרא actually enacted
steps.stepSummary: Since every opinion is really arguing about עזרא's enactment, the גמרא suggests going back to see exactly what עזרא enacted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since all the אמוראים and תנאים are arguing about עזרא's enactment, let us see how עזרא enacted it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא steps back from the details to ask what the original rule of עזרא was, and the next steps will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier opinions about forty סאה and nine קבין are different readings of one enactment by עזרא. If we know what he actually enacted, we can see where each later opinion fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all
עזרא הסופר, who enacted that a בעל קרי must immerse
Enacted, set up a rabbinic rule
Let us see, let us look

phrases.english: Since all the Amoraim and Tannaim
are arguing about Ezra's enactment,
let us see how Ezra enacted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי כּוּלְּהוּ אָמוֹרָאֵי וְתַנָּאֵי בִּדְעֶזְרָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from specific rulings to the root enactment behind them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly did עזרא enact for a בעל קרי?

steps.title: אביי: עזרא made two rules for a healthy person
steps.stepSummary: אביי says עזרא enacted forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission and nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: עזרא enacted forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission, and nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by describing what עזרא enacted. In his view, both amounts come from עזרא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's view, עזרא already split the healthy person (בריא) into two cases. A normal emission needs full immersion in forty סאה. An involuntary emission needs only nine קבין poured over him.

keyTerms.meaning: A healthy person
Forty סאה, the size of a full מקוה for immersion
Nine קבין of water poured over the person

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה,
phrases.english: Ezra enacted forty se'ah for a healthy person with a normal emission,
and nine kav for a healthy person whose emission was involuntary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what עזרא enacted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עזרא enacted forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission and nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.

steps.title: אביי: the אמוראים argued only about a sick person
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the אמוראים argued only about a sick person. One opinion treats him like a healthy person. The other moves him one level down, so a normal emission needs nine קבין and an involuntary one needs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אמוראים came and argued about a sick person. One held: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The other held: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his history. Since עזרא only spoke about a healthy person, the later dispute among the אמוראים was about a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives the sick person the same two levels as a healthy person. The second opinion makes a sick person's condition count like an involuntary emission. So a normal emission for him needs only nine קבין, and an involuntary one needs nothing, which matches רב אסי in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue, disagree
One master holds

phrases.english: And the Amoraim came and argued about a sick person.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל
phrases.english: One master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission,
and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא לְאוֹנְסוֹ,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission,
phrases.notes: So he needs only nine קבין poured over him.

phrases.english: and a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתוֹ אָמוֹרָאֵי וּפְלִיגִי בְּחוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's history, explaining where the later dispute fits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אמוראים argued only about a sick person: he is either treated like a healthy person, or moved one level down.

steps.title: רבא: עזרא never enacted pouring
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי. There is a tradition that עזרא enacted only immersion, so the nine-קבין pouring could not have come from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Granted that עזרא enacted immersion, but did he enact pouring? Didn't the master say: עזרא enacted immersion for those who had an emission?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's claim that the nine-קבין pouring came from עזרא. He cites a known tradition that עזרא enacted only טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gave עזרא two rules: immersion and pouring. The tradition says only 'עזרא enacted טבילה,' with no mention of pouring (נתינה). So the nine-קבין rule must have come from someone later.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that, let's accept that
Immersion in a מקוה
Pouring water over the person
Men who had a seminal emission

phrases.english: Rava said:
Granted that Ezra enacted immersion,
did he enact pouring?!
But didn't the master say:
Ezra enacted immersion for those who had an emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּתַקֵּן עֶזְרָא טְבִילָה נְתִינָה מִי תַּקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's claim that the nine קבין came from עזרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that עזרא enacted nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The known tradition says עזרא enacted only immersion, so pouring cannot be part of his enactment.

steps.title: רבא: עזרא enacted forty סאה, and later רבנן added nine קבין
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new history. עזרא enacted only forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission. Later רבנן added nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: עזרא enacted immersion in forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission. Then רבנן came and enacted nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אביי's version, רבא gives his own timeline of how the rules developed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now עזרא's enactment is only immersion, which fits the tradition. The nine-קבין pouring is a later enactment by רבנן, made only for a healthy person with an involuntary emission.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introduces a new explanation
And they enacted
The חכמים who came after עזרא

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן טְבִילָה לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה.
phrases.english: Ezra enacted immersion in forty se'ah for a healthy person with a normal emission.
And the Rabbis came and enacted
nine kav for a healthy person whose emission was involuntary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא עֶזְרָא תַּקֵּן טְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge by replacing אביי's timeline.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical reconstruction: splitting the rules between עזרא and later רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both forty סאה and nine קבין came from עזרא (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: Only forty סאה came from עזרא. The nine קבין were added later by רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. For אביי, the nine קבין come from עזרא. For רבא, they come from later רבנן.

steps.title: רבא: the Amoraim's dispute about a sick person
steps.stepSummary: In רבא's version, the אמוראים then argued about a sick person. One opinion treats him like a healthy person. The other gives forty סאה only to a healthy person with a normal emission, nine קבין to a sick person with a normal emission, and nothing to a sick person with an involuntary one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the אמוראים came and argued about a sick person. One held: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission, and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The other held: a healthy person with a normal emission needs forty סאה, a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission and needs nine קבין, but a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his timeline. After עזרא and רבנן, the אמוראים argued about how to treat a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is the same as in אביי's version, but now it builds on a mix of rules from עזרא and from רבנן. The second opinion moves the sick person one level down, which matches רב אסי's ruling that a sick person with an involuntary emission needs nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They are arguing

phrases.english: And the Amoraim came and argued about a sick person.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר חוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל,
phrases.english: One master holds: a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with a normal emission,
and a sick person with an involuntary emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר לְבָרִיא הַמַּרְגִּיל אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: for a healthy person with a normal emission, forty se'ah;

phrases.aramaic: וְחוֹלֶה הַמַּרְגִּיל כְּבָרִיא לְאוֹנְסוֹ — תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין.
phrases.english: and a sick person with a normal emission is like a healthy person with an involuntary emission: nine kav.
But a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתוֹ אָמוֹרָאֵי וְקָא מִיפַּלְגִי בְּחוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's timeline by placing the dispute of the אמוראים after עזרא and רבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבא: עזרא enacted forty סאה, רבנן added nine קבין, and the אמוראים argued whether a sick person is like a healthy one or one level lower.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three layers in רבא's version. עזרא enacted forty סאה for a healthy person with a normal emission. רבנן added nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission. The אמוראים argued about a sick person, and in the lenient opinion, a sick person with an involuntary emission needs nothing.

steps.title: רבא's practical ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: a בריא or חולה with a normal emission needs forty סאה, a בריא with an involuntary emission needs nine קבין, and a חולה with an involuntary emission needs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that a healthy person with a normal emission and a sick person with a normal emission need forty סאה. A healthy person with an involuntary emission needs nine קבין. But a sick person with an involuntary emission is exempt from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the history and argument, רבא now tells us the bottom-line halacha in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person with a normal emission is treated just like a healthy person and needs forty סאה. Only the sick person with an involuntary emission is let off completely. So the ruling has three levels: forty סאה, nine קבין, and nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha, meaning the practical ruling
A healthy person
A sick person
One whose emission came in the normal way
One whose emission was involuntary, not by choice
Exempt from anything; no purification needed

steps.whatToRemember: Final halacha: normal emission, healthy or sick, needs forty סאה. Healthy and involuntary needs nine קבין. Sick and involuntary needs nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the sick person always gets a lighter law. With a normal emission he needs the full forty סאה. Only when he is both sick and the emission was involuntary is he fully exempt.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is:
A healthy person with a normal emission and a sick person with a normal emission
need forty se'a.
And a healthy person with an involuntary emission needs nine kav.
But a sick person with an involuntary emission
is exempt from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the history-and-dispute section of steps 4-8 with the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Forty סאה for any normal emission, nine קבין for a healthy person with an involuntary emission, and nothing for a sick person with an involuntary emission.

steps.title: A teaching on nine קבין for oneself and forty סאה for others
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says nine קבין of water makes a בעל קרי pure for his own learning, but teaching others needs forty סאה. רבי יהודה says forty סאה is always required.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A בעל קרי who had nine קבין of water poured over him is pure. When is this said? For himself. But for others, he needs forty סאה. רבי יהודה says: Forty סאה in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, that adds a split between learning Torah on your own and teaching it to others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives two levels. Nine קבין is enough to learn for yourself, but teaching others needs a full forty סאה. רבי יהודה rejects the light option and always demands forty סאה. This sets up the two disputes that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; it introduces a ברייתא
A man who had a seminal emission
For himself, meaning learning Torah on his own
For others, meaning teaching Torah to others
In any case, no matter what

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A man who had an emission, on whom they poured
nine kav of water, is pure.
When are these words said? For himself,
phrases.notes: "For himself" means learning Torah on his own. "For others" in the next line means teaching them.

phrases.english: but for others, forty se'a.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Forty se'a in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new source on the same topic and adds the distinction between learning alone and teaching others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine קבין purifies for learning alone, and forty סאה is needed to teach others. רבי יהודה requires forty סאה always.

steps.title: Dispute over the first part: does teaching others always need forty סאה?
steps.stepSummary: Four אמוראים form two pairs. One from each pair argues about the first part of the ברייתא. One says forty סאה for teaching applies only to a sick person with a normal emission. The other says anyone teaching needs forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי, and רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: one from this pair and one from that pair argued about the first part. One said: What you said, 'For himself, but for others forty סאה,' was taught only about a sick person with a normal emission. But a sick person with an involuntary emission needs only nine קבין. And one said: Anyone teaching others, even a sick person with an involuntary emission, is not pure until there are forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names four אמוראים and reports the first of two disputes. This one is about how far the ברייתא's demand of forty סאה for teaching others goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion limits the forty סאה rule to a sick person with a normal emission. A sick person with an involuntary emission can teach after nine קבין. The second opinion says the teaching rule has no exceptions: anyone who teaches others needs forty סאה. The גמרא does not tell us which אמורא held which view.

keyTerms.meaning: A pair
The first part of a teaching
They taught it only about; this limits a rule

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

phrases.aramaic: חַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: One from this pair and one from that pair argued about the first part.
One said: That which you said,
"When are these words said? For himself,
but for others, forty se'a,"
was taught only about a sick person with a normal emission,
but a sick person with an involuntary emission needs nine kav.
And one said: Anyone teaching others,
even a sick person with an involuntary emission,
is not pure until there are forty se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the first part of the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view says forty סאה for teaching applies only to a sick person with a normal emission. The other says anyone teaching others needs forty סאה.

steps.title: Dispute over the last part: does רבי יהודה's forty סאה work in vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The other two אמוראים argue about רבי יהודה's forty סאה. One says it must be water in the ground. The other says forty סאה in vessels also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one from this pair and one from that pair argued about the last part. One said: What רבי יהודה said, 'Forty סאה in any case,' was taught only about water in the ground, but not in vessels. And one said: Even in vessels too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports the second dispute. This one is about what kind of forty סאה רבי יהודה requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says רבי יהודה means a real מקוה, water standing in the ground. Forty סאה gathered in containers would not count. The other view says even forty סאה held in vessels is enough for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
The ground, meaning a pool in the earth like a מקוה
Vessels or containers

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two parts each cause a dispute. The first is about who must use forty סאה to teach. The second is about whether רבי יהודה's forty סאה must be in the ground or can be in vessels.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַסֵּיפָא.
phrases.english: And one from this pair and one from that pair argued about the last part.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הָא דְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: One said: That which Rabbi Yehuda said,
"forty se'a in any case,"
was taught only about water in the ground,
but in vessels, no.
And one said: Even in vessels too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא וְחַד מֵהַאי זוּגָא אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the first part of the ברייתא to רבי יהודה's view in the last part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view limits רבי יהודה's forty סאה to water in the ground. The other accepts forty סאה in vessels too.

steps.title: What does 'in any case' add for the opinion that requires ground water?
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that forty סאה in vessels is acceptable fits רבי יהודה's words 'מכל מקום' well. For the opinion that only ground water works, the גמרא asks what 'מכל מקום' comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says forty סאה works even in vessels: that is why רבי יהודה says 'forty סאה in any case.' But for the one who says only water in the ground works and not water in vessels, what does 'in any case' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opinion from step 12 that רבי יהודה requires the forty סאה to be water in the ground. It asks how that opinion explains his words 'מכל מקום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מכל מקום' sounds like it widens the rule to include something unexpected. For the lenient opinion, that something is water in vessels. The strict opinion rules out vessels, so the גמרא asks what extra case the word could be adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (fine for one side, but a problem for the other)
In any case / in every situation
Vessels / containers
The ground
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said: even in vessels
that is why it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מִכׇּל מָקוֹם״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: 'Forty se'a in any case.'
But according to the one who said: in the ground, yes,
in vessels, no,
what does 'in any case' come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֲפִילּוּ בְּכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the strict opinion from step 12 against the wording of רבי יהודה in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that רבי יהודה requires the forty סאה to be water in the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra phrase 'מכל מקום' seems to have nothing to include once vessels are ruled out.

steps.title: It includes drawn water
steps.stepSummary: 'מכל מקום' comes to include מים שאובין, water drawn by people and collected in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include drawn water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Even for the strict opinion, 'מכל מקום' adds something: drawn water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water drawn by human hand normally does not count for a מקוה. According to this answer, רבי יהודה is lenient here: forty סאה sitting in the ground works for a בעל קרי even if people drew it. So the phrase still has a job, and the strict opinion stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawn water, meaning water collected by people using containers

phrases.english: To include drawn water.
phrases.notes: This is water people carried over in buckets, which normally doesn't count for a מקוה. Here it's fine as long as it sits in the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוּיֵי מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new case to include
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought 'מכל מקום' could only mean water in vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מכל מקום' includes drawn water collected in the ground, so the strict opinion is fine.
steps.whatToRemember: For the opinion that רבי יהודה requires ground water, 'מכל מקום' means even מים שאובין count.

steps.title: רב פפא asks to lead ברכת המזון because nine קבין fell on him
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and רבא בר רבי בר שמואל ate together. רב פפא asked to lead ברכת המזון because he had purified himself with nine קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, רב הונא the son of רב יהושע, and רבא בר רבי בר שמואל ate bread together. רב פפא said to them: Let me lead the ברכה, since nine קבין of water fell on me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that shows the rules about a בעל קרי in action. רב פפא claims the right to lead ברכת המזון because he purified himself with nine קבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumes that nine קבין is enough to make him fit to lead others in a ברכה. This sets up the next step, where his friend questions whether nine קבין is enough when you act for others.

keyTerms.meaning: They ate a meal together (literally, 'wrapped bread')
Give me (the honor)
To lead the blessing, meaning ברכת המזון for the group
Upon me

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua
and Rava son of Rabbi bar Shmuel
ate bread together.
phrases.notes: Literally 'wrapped bread.' It's an expression for sharing a meal.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
Give me the chance to lead the blessing,
since nine kav fell upon me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרָבָא בְּרַבִּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרִיכוּ רִיפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discussing the ברייתא to a story about acting on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא considers nine קבין enough to lead others in ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רבא בר רבי בר שמואל objects that acting for others needs forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רבי בר שמואל quotes the ברייתא: nine קבין is only enough for oneself, and for others forty סאה is needed. Since he had immersed in forty סאה, he should lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רבי בר שמואל said to them: We learned, when is this rule said? For himself. But for others, forty סאה is needed. So let me lead the ברכה, since forty סאה fell on me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב פפא using the ברייתא from step 10. He then claims the honor for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says nine קבין is enough only for oneself, and serving others requires forty סאה. רבא בר רבי בר שמואל treats leading others in ברכת המזון like teaching others. Since he immersed in a full forty סאה, he says he is the fitting one to lead.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a ברייתא)
When is this rule said? (introduces a limit on the rule)
For himself
For others

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא בְּרַבִּי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rava son of Rabbi bar Shmuel said to them:
We learned: When is this said? For himself,
but for others, forty se'a.
Rather, give me the chance to lead the blessing,
since forty se'a fell upon me.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנֵינָא, בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's claim from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that nine קבין lets him lead others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits nine קבין to oneself. Acting for others requires forty סאה.

steps.title: רב הונא never became impure at all
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he should lead, since he needed neither nine קבין nor forty סאה. He never became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: Let me lead the ברכה, since neither this nor that is upon me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא tops both of his friends. He has the best claim because he never needed any purification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier claims rested on fixing an impurity. רב הונא points out that someone who stayed pure the whole time is better than anyone who had to purify himself, whatever the amount of water.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither this nor that

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to them:
Give me the chance to lead the blessing,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵיכָּא עִילָּוַאי לָא הַאי וְלָא הַאי.
phrases.english: since there is upon me neither this nor that.
phrases.notes: He means he never became impure, so he needed neither the nine קבין nor the forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא: הַבוּ לִי לְדִידִי לִבְרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the friendly contest by claiming a level higher than both previous claims.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who never became impure is the most fitting to lead.

steps.title: רב חמא immersed on ערב פסח for the public
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא used to immerse on ערב פסח so he could help the public fulfill their obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא would immerse on the day before פסח in order to help the public fulfill their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another practice: רב חמא immersed before פסח so he could act for the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא בר רבי בר שמואל in step 16, רב חמא holds that acting on behalf of others calls for a full immersion. He did it on ערב פסח because on פסח he would be helping many people fulfill their obligations.

keyTerms.meaning: Would immerse
The day before פסח
To help the public fulfill their obligation

phrases.aramaic: רַב חָמָא טָבֵיל בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִסְחָא
phrases.english: Rav Chama would immerse on the eve of Pesach
to help the public fulfill their obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָמָא טָבֵיל בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְפִסְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example of the idea that acting for others needs a higher level of purity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא immersed before פסח in order to act on behalf of the public.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב חמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רב חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the section by rejecting רב חמא's practice as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא's practice treated acting for others as needing extra purity. The גמרא says the הלכה does not follow him, so this distinction between oneself and others is not accepted in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is not like him

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the practice described in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה does not follow רב חמא's extra immersion for acting on behalf of others.
steps.whatToRemember: The stories show the idea that serving others needs more purity, but the הלכה does not follow רב חמא's practice.

steps.title: Remembering in the middle of prayer: shorten, don't stop
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person who remembers during תפלה that he is a בעל קרי should not stop. He should shorten his prayer instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone was standing in the middle of תפלה and remembered that he is a בעל קרי, he should not stop. Instead he should shorten his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case: a person is already davening and suddenly realizes he is a בעל קרי. The משנה tells him to finish quickly rather than stop in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally a בעל קרי should not daven at all, but once he has started, the משנה does not want him to break off. The compromise is to shorten each ברכה and finish.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the abbreviation מַתְנִי׳ marks where the משנה begins)
A man who had a seminal emission and has not yet immersed
He should not stop or interrupt
He should shorten (his prayer)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one was standing in prayer
and remembered that he had a seminal emission,
he should not stop, but rather shorten.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion about בעל קרי and immersion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי who remembers his status during תפלה finishes his prayer in a shortened form instead of stopping.

steps.title: Immersing near sunrise: saying שמע in the water if needed
steps.stepSummary: Someone who went into the water to immerse should come out, get dressed, and say שמע if there is time before sunrise. If there is no time, he covers himself with the water and says שמע there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone went down to immerse and he has time to come up, get dressed, and say שמע before sunrise, he should do that. If not, he should cover himself with the water and say שמע right there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: a person is in the water immersing and the deadline for שמע (sunrise) is close. It tells him how to say שמע in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal is to say שמע properly dressed, outside the water. If waiting would make him miss the time, the water itself can count as a covering, so he may say שמע while standing in it.

keyTerms.meaning: To immerse (in a מקוה)
To cover oneself (with clothing)
Sunrise, the ideal deadline for the morning שמע
And if not

phrases.english: If he went down to immerse,
if he is able to go up and cover himself

phrases.aramaic: וְלִקְרוֹת עַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה —
phrases.english: and recite before sunrise —
phrases.notes: "Recite" here means saying the morning שמע.

phrases.english: he should go up, cover himself, and recite,
and if not —
he should cover himself in the water and recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרַד לִטְבּוֹל, אִם יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת וּלְהִתְכַּסּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה moves from תפלה to the related case of קריאת שמע while immersing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If there is time, he comes out, dresses, and says שמע. If not, he says שמע covered by the water.

steps.title: Not in foul water, and four אמות from foul things
steps.stepSummary: Covering oneself with water does not work if the water is foul or used for soaking flax, unless fresh water is poured in. One must also keep four אמות away from such things and from צואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he may not cover himself in foul water or in water used for soaking flax, unless he pours fresh water into it. And how far must he keep from them and from feces? Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the previous rule: not every water may serve as a covering for שמע. It ends with a general distance rule of four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foul-smelling water is not a fitting place to say holy words, so it cannot serve as his covering unless clean water is added. The משנה then sets a general rule: keep four אמות from bad-smelling things and צואה when saying שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Foul, bad-smelling water
Water used for soaking flax, which smells bad
Excrement, feces
Four cubits, roughly two meters

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three rules: shorten תפלה if you remember mid-prayer, say שמע in clean water if time is short, and keep four אמות from foul things.

phrases.english: But he may not cover himself in foul water
nor in soaking water,
until he pours water into them.
And how far must he distance himself from them and from feces —
four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה לֹא בַּמַּיִם הָרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the previous rule: only clean water may serve as a covering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foul or soaking water may not be used as a covering unless fresh water is added. One must keep four אמות from foul things and צואה.

steps.title: ברייתא adds קריאת התורה: read on with a quick voice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the משנה's rule about תפלה. It adds that a person reading from the תורה who remembers he is a בעל קרי does not stop, but reads on quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: If someone was standing in prayer and remembered he is a בעל קרי, he should not stop, but shorten. If someone was reading the תורה and remembered he is a בעל קרי, he does not stop and get up. Instead he reads on in a quick, mumbled voice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts with the same rule as the משנה. It then adds a parallel case of reading from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about תפלה. The ברייתא extends the same idea to קריאת התורה: once he has started, he keeps going, but in a hurried, less careful way.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה (the abbreviation גְּמָ׳ marks where it begins)
The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
Reading from the תורה
Reads quickly or mumbles, without careful pronunciation

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
If one was standing in prayer
and remembered that he had a seminal emission —
he should not stop, but rather shorten.
If one was reading the Torah
and remembered that he had a seminal emission —
he does not stop and get up,
but rather reads on quickly and keeps reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports the משנה's first rule and adds a parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי who remembers during קריאת התורה keeps reading quickly instead of stopping.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: no more than three פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees and limits a בעל קרי to reading at most three פסוקים from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A בעל קרי is not allowed to read more than three פסוקים in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the same ברייתא, רבי מאיר gives a different opinion about the קריאת התורה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion let him keep reading in a quick voice. רבי מאיר sets a firm limit: three פסוקים, the smallest amount that counts as a valid reading, and then he must stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, allowed
Three verses, the minimum for one person's reading

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
One who had a seminal emission is not permitted
to read in the Torah
more than three verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין בַּעַל קֶרִי רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא about the קריאת התורה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a בעל קרי may read no more than three פסוקים.

steps.title: צואה in front of you: walk forward past it
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that if someone praying sees צואה in front of him, he walks forward until it is four אמות behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: If someone was standing in prayer and saw feces in front of him, he walks forward until it is four cubits behind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's last rule, about distance from צואה. It brings a ברייתא with a specific instruction for someone already davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the distance, four אמות. This ברייתא says how to get that distance in the middle of davening: move forward until the צואה is four אמות behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
In front of him
Behind him

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
If one was standing in prayer
and saw feces in front of him —
he walks forward
until he places it four cubits behind him.
phrases.notes: Literally "until he throws it behind him." He doesn't touch it; he walks past it so it ends up behind him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְרָאָה צוֹאָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בעל קרי rules to the משנה's rule about distance from צואה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone praying who sees צואה ahead walks forward until it is four אמות behind him.

steps.title: But another ברייתא says to the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with another ברייתא, which says it is enough to move four אמות to the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא that moving to the side is enough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two ברייתות. One says to walk forward past the צואה, and the other says moving to the side is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If stepping to the side is enough, why would the first ברייתא require walking all the way past the צואה? The two sources seem to give different rules for the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught? (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)
To the sides

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: to the sides?
phrases.notes: This is short for a ברייתא saying he may move four אמות to the side instead of forward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא לִצְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 25 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא requiring him to walk forward until the צואה is four אמות behind him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says moving to the side is enough, which seems to make walking forward unnecessary.

steps.title: Forward when possible, to the side when not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Walking forward is required when it is possible; moving to the side is for when walking forward is not possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This ברייתא is talking about when it is possible to walk forward, and that ברייתא is talking about when it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking forward so the צואה ends up behind him is the preferred way. Moving to the side is a fallback for when he cannot go forward, so the two ברייתות do not really argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... that one; each source refers to a different case
Possible

steps.whatToRemember: When praying, the best way to distance yourself from צואה is to move forward until it is four אמות behind you. If that cannot be done, moving four אמות to the side is enough.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it is possible,
that is where it is not possible.
phrases.notes: "Possible" means possible to walk forward. The "forward" ברייתא is when he can; the "side" ברייתא is when he can't.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא, דְּאֶפְשָׁר, הָא, דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give conflicting rules for the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Walk forward when possible; move to the side only when walking forward is not possible.

steps.title: רבה: a prayer said near feces still counts
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that someone who prayed and then found צואה in his spot did wrong, but his תפלה is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone was praying and found feces in his spot, רבה said: even though he sinned, his prayer is still a prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: a person finished praying and discovered צואה where he stood. רבה says the תפלה still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps covered seeing צואה before or during תפלה. Here the person only finds out afterward. רבה separates two things: the person did something wrong, but the תפלה itself is not cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Feces. One may not pray near it.
In his place, the spot where he stood to pray
Even though he sinned
His prayer is a prayer, meaning it counts

phrases.english: If one was praying
and found feces in his place,
Rabba said:
Even though he sinned —
his prayer is a prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל וּמָצָא צוֹאָה בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of seeing צואה during תפלה to the case of discovering it only after praying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person sinned, but his תפלה is valid after the fact.

steps.title: רבא's challenge: the offering of the wicked is disgusting
steps.stepSummary: רבא attacks רבה's ruling with the פסוק "זבח רשעים תועבה".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: But it says, "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבה with a פסוק. If the person sinned, how can his תפלה be accepted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that a קרבן brought by a sinner is rejected, not accepted. רבא applies the same idea to תפלה: a prayer offered through a sin cannot count as a good prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged him, raised a strong objection
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination

phrases.english: Rava challenged him:
But isn't it written:
"The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination"!

steps.confusionAlert: רַבָּה (with a ה) and רָבָא (with an א) are two different אמוראים who often argue. Here רבה makes the ruling and רבא challenges it.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the תפלה counts even though he sinned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that a קרבן connected to sin is rejected. תפלה is like a קרבן, so a תפלה said while sinning should be rejected too.

steps.title: רבא's ruling: such a prayer is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the opposite ruling: because he sinned, his תפלה is an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Since he sinned, even though he prayed, his prayer is an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבה's view, רבא states his own rule. The תפלה does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reverses רבה's sentence. רבה said "even though he sinned, it counts." רבא says "since he sinned, even though he prayed, it is a תועבה." The sin cancels the value of the תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces a replacement view.
Since, because
Abomination, something disgusting

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: the תפלה counts even though he sinned. רבא: because he sinned, the תפלה is a תועבה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Since he sinned,
even though he prayed —
his prayer is an abomination.
phrases.notes: So it doesn't count, and he has to pray again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְחָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his challenge, רבא replaces רבה's ruling with his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תפלה said in a place with צואה, through the person's own fault, is a תועבה and does not count.

steps.title: ברייתא: stop praying while urine drips
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone with urine dripping on his knees during תפלה stops until it ends and then resumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone was standing in prayer and urine was dripping on his knees, he stops until the urine finishes, and then goes back and prays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about an interruption in the middle of תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says two things. He must stop while the urine is flowing, and afterward he continues praying. It does not say where in the תפלה he restarts, and the next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
Dripping, flowing
He stops, interrupts
And goes back and prays

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one was standing in prayer
and water was dripping on his knees —
phrases.notes: "Water" is a polite way of saying urine.

phrases.english: he stops until the water finishes
and goes back and prays.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, an interruption during תפלה, after finishing the צואה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone with urine dripping during תפלה stops until it ends and then resumes praying.

steps.title: Where does he pick up again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks to what point in the תפלה he returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where does he return?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's words "he goes back and prays."
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Goes back and prays" is unclear. It could mean starting the whole תפלה over, or just continuing from where he stopped. The גמרא wants to pin this down.

keyTerms.meaning: To where?

phrases.english: To where does he return?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהֵיכָן חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the ברייתא's phrase "וחוזר ומתפלל."
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether resuming means restarting the תפלה from the beginning or continuing from the point where he stopped.

steps.title: Two views: from the beginning, or from where he stopped
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree. One says he returns to the beginning, the other says to where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagreed: one said he goes back to the beginning, and one said he goes back to the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no single answer. One view treats the interruption as breaking the תפלה, so he must start again from the beginning. The other lets him simply continue from where he stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: One said
Returns to the beginning
To the place where he stopped

phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna:
one said he returns to the beginning,
and one said:
to the place where he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32 with a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a disagreement: one view says he returns to the beginning of the תפלה, the other says to the point where he stopped.

steps.title: Suggesting the root of their disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to suggest that the two אמוראים disagree because of a deeper issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they disagree about this:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to propose what the real reason behind the disagreement is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לימא" introduces a suggestion, not a final answer. The גמרא will try to connect this disagreement to a known, broader dispute, and that suggestion may later be accepted or pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion.
They disagree

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the disagreement from step 33 and starts searching for its underlying reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What deeper principle explains why רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree about where he resumes.
